definitions: To resent or blame someone for something they have done.
To allow a past action or mistake to negatively influence one's opinion or treatment of someone.
examples: I don't hold it against him that he made a mistake.
She still holds it against me that I forgot her birthday.
Don't hold it against them; they didn't know any better.
pastTenses: held it against (past simple), has/have held it against (present perfect), held it against (past perfect)
